newsitem.title: USA: Salomon same-store sales index up 2.4 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Salomon same-store sales index up 2.4 pct in May.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said Thursday its same-store retail sales index rose 2.4 percent in May, compared with a 3.6 percent gain in April and a 5.2 percent increase a year ago.
Same-store sales are sales of stores that are open at least one year.

"On balance, results were modestly below expectations as a result of cold and wet weather during the month," Salomon Brothers said in a research note. "While inventories are on the high side, we believe that with potentially more seasonable weather and reduced purchases, levels will become more in line with sales trends by mid to late June."

Salomon Brothers also said that it thinks strong inventory and expense controls will lead to retailers' earnings outpacing the average earnings of the S&P 500 beginning in the second, or at the latest, third quarter of 1997, despite the recent strength in stock prices for the group.

Among major retailers, shares in Wal-Mart Stores Inc were up 1/8 at 31 Thursday, Sears, Roebuck and Co was unchanged at 49, Dayton Hudson Corp was up 1-1/2 at 52-1/4, Kmart Corp down 11/32 at 13-5/32 and Federated Department Stores Inc up 1/8 at 36-1/4.
